newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First's Henare repeats won't work with National.
newsitem.headline: NZ First's Henare repeats won't work with National.

text.p: New Zealand First Party deputy leader Tau Henare reiterated on Monday that he was not willing to work with the National Party in a coalition after the October 12 general election.
Henare said, however, that the decision on any coalition would be taken by the party's caucus.

"I am bound by the decision of my caucus and I am behind my caucus 100 percent, so that would mean if New Zealand First decided to get into a coalition with National, then I would certainly play a very, very minor role and a backbench role," he told Radio New Zealand.
New Zealand First leader Winston Peters told Reuters on Sunday that Henare's opposition to a deal with National was a personal view.

"This (NZ First) is a big party and it will be the biggest in the country come election day and this (decision on a coalition partner) is an initiative that will be taken by the membership of New Zealand First. That is why we can promise when we have taken a decision democratically it will bind us for the next three years," Peters said.
He added: "I haven't slaved and made enormous sacrifices...to then rush along and put Mr Bolger back in power. We are out to win in our own right.
"This is the script and it comes from the leader. We are going to win by far the greatest number of seats in Parliament and then the questions you are raising now will simply not matter."
Asked if he would step down if the caucus voted to go into coalition with a Bolger-led National Party, Peters said he would go with the democratic decison.

"I have to say as some sort of pointer I can't see too many people rushing to join the National Party after the election. Why would we? They have brought this country economically and socially, in terms of eight out of ten New Zealanders, to its knees. So why would you rush to repeat that experiment for the next three years?"
He said he believed National would lose the election and it would then not be worried about the fate of Bolger, Birch and Shipley.
"I have been in the National Party a long time and I know what the outcome will be for those people the day after the election," Peters said.
Peters was sacked as Maori Affairs Minister from Bolger's government. He left National in 1992 to form New Zealand First.
